confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors rest on aggregated cost-of-living data found in search. Numbeo data (snapshot 1 June 2026, republished by Expatica) gave about £15.18 for an inexpensive meal, £3.46 for a cappuccino and £5.31 for a 0.5 L draught beer. Expatistan listed a cappuccino at about £2.88 and a pub beer at about £5.35. Published UK pint averages are about £5.34 to £5.50. Midrange_meal_2p was not found directly for Cardiff, so it is a bounded estimate from the inexpensive-meal price and general UK mid-range pricing. Cocktail rests on an Expatistan figure of about £9 for a downtown club (about nine price points). Wine by the glass is a typical UK restaurant price scaled against beer, since the one venue menu found (The Ivy Asia, from £9.50) was not a city average. I assumed roughly 1.34 USD per GBP for conversion, which I did not search, so all USD anchors carry that uncertainty. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for a Cardiff summer window. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. The FX figure comes from a search-result summary of the RBA exchange rates page, not a direct page read. It showed 0.6720 USD per AUD for 18 November 2026, which I did not verify further.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cardiff is treated as a mid-sized UK regional capital, priced slightly below the UK average for eating out. Numbeo-based data put eating out about 2% below the UK average. It is cheaper than London and similar to cities such as Bristol or Manchester, though somewhat cheaper for drinks. A Nation.Cymru study also placed Welsh cities among the cheaper UK locations for a night out.
